344:                 labels = labels[: last_idx[0, 0]]
345:             # Clip to the range (-inf, t_max)
346:             intervals = intervals[: last_idx[0, 0]]
347: 
348:         intervals = np.minimum(t_max, intervals)
349: 
350:         if intervals.max() < t_max:
351:             # Last boundary is below t_max: add a new boundary and label
352:             intervals = np.vstack((intervals, [intervals.max(), t_max]))
353:             if labels is not None:
354:                 labels.append(end_label)
355: 
356:     return intervals, labels
357: 
358: 
359: def adjust_events(events, labels=None, t_min=0.0, t_max=None, label_prefix="__"):
360:     """Adjust the given list of event times to span the range
361:     ``[t_min, t_max]``.
362: 
363:     Any event times outside of the specified range will be removed.
364: 
365:     If the times do not span ``[t_min, t_max]``, additional events will be
366:     added with the prefix ``label_prefix``.
367: 
368:     Parameters
369:     ----------
370:     events : np.ndarray
371:         Array of event times (seconds)
372:     labels : list or None
373:         List of labels
374:         (Default value = None)
375:     t_min : float or None
376:         Minimum valid event time.
377:         (Default value = 0.0)
378:     t_max : float or None
379:         Maximum valid event time.
380:         (Default value = None)
381:     label_prefix : str
382:         Prefix string to use for synthetic labels
383:         (Default value = '__')
384: 
385:     Returns
386:     -------
387:     new_times : np.ndarray
388:         Event times corrected to the given range.
389: 
390:     """
391:     if t_min is not None:
392:         first_idx = np.argwhere(events >= t_min)
393: 
394:         if len(first_idx) > 0:
395:             # We have events below t_min
396:             # Crop them out
397:             if labels is not None:
398:                 labels = labels[first_idx[0, 0] :]
399:             events = events[first_idx[0, 0] :]
400: 
401:         if events[0] > t_min:
402:             # Lowest boundary is higher than t_min:
403:             # add a new boundary and label
404:             events = np.concatenate(([t_min], events))
405:             if labels is not None:
406:                 labels.insert(0, "%sT_MIN" % label_prefix)
407: 
408:     if t_max is not None:
409:         last_idx = np.argwhere(events > t_max)
410: 
411:         if len(last_idx) > 0:
412:             # We have boundaries above t_max.
413:             # Trim to only boundaries <= t_max
414:             if labels is not None:
415:                 labels = labels[: last_idx[0, 0]]
416:             events = events[: last_idx[0, 0]]
417: 
418:         if events[-1] < t_max:
419:             # Last boundary is below t_max: add a new boundary and label
420:             events = np.concatenate((events, [t_max]))
421:             if labels is not None:
422:                 labels.append("%sT_MAX" % label_prefix)
423: 
424:     return events, labels
425: 
426: 
427: def intersect_files(flist1, flist2):
428:     """Return the intersection of two sets of filepaths, based on the file name
429:     (after the final '/') and ignoring the file extension.
430: 
431:     Examples
432:     --------
433:      >>> flist1 = ['/a/b/abc.lab', '/c/d/123.lab', '/e/f/xyz.lab']
434:      >>> flist2 = ['/g/h/xyz.npy', '/i/j/123.txt', '/k/l/456.lab']
435:      >>> sublist1, sublist2 = mir_eval.util.intersect_files(flist1, flist2)
436:      >>> print sublist1
437:      ['/e/f/xyz.lab', '/c/d/123.lab']
438:      >>> print sublist2
439:      ['/g/h/xyz.npy', '/i/j/123.txt']
440: 
441:     Parameters
442:     ----------
443:     flist1 : list
444:         first list of filepaths
445:     flist2 : list
446:         second list of filepaths
447: 
448:     Returns
449:     -------
450:     sublist1 : list
451:         subset of filepaths with matching stems from ``flist1``
452:     sublist2 : list
453:         corresponding filepaths from ``flist2``
454: 
455:     """
456: 
457:     def fname(abs_path):
458:         """Return the filename given an absolute path.
459: 
460:         Parameters
461:         ----------
462:         abs_path
463: 
464:         Returns
465:         -------
466:         filename
467: 
468:         """
469:         return os.path.splitext(os.path.split(abs_path)[-1])[0]
470: 
471:     fmap = {fname(f): f for f in flist1}
472:     pairs = [list(), list()]
473:     for f in flist2:
474:         if fname(f) in fmap:
475:             pairs[0].append(fmap[fname(f)])
476:             pairs[1].append(f)
477: 
478:     return pairs
479: 
480: 
481: def merge_labeled_intervals(x_intervals, x_labels, y_intervals, y_labels):
482:     r"""Merge the time intervals of two sequences.
483: 
484:     Parameters
485:     ----------
486:     x_intervals : np.ndarray
487:         Array of interval times (seconds)
488:     x_labels : list or None
489:         List of labels
490:     y_intervals : np.ndarray
491:         Array of interval times (seconds)
492:     y_labels : list or None
493:         List of labels
494: 
495:     Returns
496:     -------
497:     new_intervals : np.ndarray
498:         New interval times of the merged sequences.
499:     new_x_labels : list
